title: Introduce adaptive degraded-mode operator and priority traffic triage probe
author: Maya Patel
body:
Summary:
Introduce an 'Adaptive Degraded Mode Operator' (ADMO) that centralizes runtime decisions for graceful degradation during high-pressure events, plus a lightweight 'Priority Triage Probe' that classifies burst traffic patterns and applies fast-path admission controls. This addresses recurring incidents where noisy telemetry + regional spikes caused wholesale circuit flips and unnecessary regional failovers. The change is scoped to runtime admission, telemetry sanitization, and operator-facing rollout hooks.

Motivation & Context:
- Several incidents over the last quarter (see ENG-4421) showed cascading circuit resets during short, tenant-localized bursts.
- Current heuristics conflate metric noise with genuine SLO pressure; regional failovers sometimes trigger before KV-preserve drains complete, losing hot cache and amplifying latency.
- We need a compact, explainable decision layer that: (1) deduplicates noisy telemetry, (2) fast-classifies traffic type (burst vs sustained, high-cost vs low-cost), and (3) applies a prioritized admission policy that preserves latency SLOs where possible while shedding non-essential load.

What this PR does (single-line checklist):
- Adds ADMO: a runtime operator that consumes existing health/telemetry streams and produces ranked actions (trim, soft-deny, defer, escalate).
- Adds Priority Triage Probe: an inline probe (O(100us) path) that tags inflight requests by cost profile and source cohort for fast admission rules.
- Introduces a Telemetry Sanitizer filter to smooth out high-frequency spikes from noisy clients.
- Adds a safe fallback: if ADMO becomes unreachable, the system reverts to the current static shedder config.
- Exposes operator-facing flags in ops/recipes for staggered rollout and automatic canary unfreeze.

Implementation notes / commits summary:
- commit 1: runtime/operator: new admode package + decision engine (rule interpreter + simple exp backoff scheduler).
- commit 2: serving/probe: priority triage probe integrated into request admission path; small inline fast-path hooks.
- commit 3: telemetry/filter: sanitization pipeline with configurable windowing and percentile-trimming.
- commit 4: ops/recipes: deployment manifests and rollout script to enable ADMO behind a feature flag with a staggered 10% -> 50% -> 100% rollout.
- commit 5: tests: unit tests for rule interpreter, integration test that validates fallback behaviour, and a load test script to simulate tenant-localized bursts.

Files changed (high level):
- src/serving/admission/admode.go (+admode_test.go) -- core operator and decision loop.
- src/serving/admission/probe.go (+probe_test.go) -- Priority Triage Probe, small deterministic classifier.
- pkg/telemetry/sanitizer.go -- smoothing filter and config validation.
- ops/recipes/admode-rollout.yaml -- k8s job + canary traffic split.
- infra/monitoring/dashboards/admode-overview.json -- new dashboard panels for operator decisions and triage distribution.
- tests/load/burst-simulator.go -- deterministic burst patterns used for integration.
- docs/observability/admode.md -- operator playbook and debugging steps.
- ci/flakeguard.yaml -- add test flake guard for burst-simulator to reduce CI noise.

Behavioral guarantees and safety: (important)
- No breaking changes to API surface. ADMO runs behind a feature flag by default (off).
- When enabled, ADMO makes only non-destructive decisions (soft-deny / priority tag). The system will never evict tenant state; full evictions remain operator-controlled.
- If ADMO fails health checks, an automatic reversion to the static shedder occurs within 10s.

Review notes and decisions:
- Performance: The probe path is <150ns additional median overhead in microbenchmarks; see tests/load results included. We intentionally keep the probe classifier deterministic and tiny to avoid GC pressure.
- Explainability: ADMO decision logs include a decision-context payload (cohort, recent-latency-p95, kv-pressure-ratio) to help on-call triage.
- Telemetry: The sanitizer defaults are conservative (window=30s, trim=95th->80th mapping) but can be tuned via config.

Review conversation (excerpted, chronological):
- Evan Zhao (reviewer): "Looks good overall; need stronger invariants around 'admode unreachable' fallback to avoid split-brain where half the cluster thinks ADMO is on and half off."
- Author (Maya): "Added a liveness fence and a quorum check in admode.go; ADMO toggles only after a 3/5 coordinator quorum window. See admode.go:Start() changes."
- Evan: "Please include a small integration test showing fallback behavior and a CI job to exercise it."
- Author: "Added tests/load/burst-fallback_test.go and wired it into ci/flakeguard. Reran CI."
- Priya Menon (reviewer): "Telemetry sanitization looks reasonable, but we should surface the sanitizer's applied-trim metric to dashboards."
- Author: "Added applied_trim gauge and dashboard panel in infra/monitoring/dashboards/admode-overview.json."
- Liam O'Connor (approver): "Approving after seeing canary rollout recipe and the integration tests pass."

CI and validation history: 
- Initial CI run (unit + lint): failed on go vet in admode.go (unsafe nil-check). Fixed in commit 2.
- Second CI run (unit + integration): flake in burst-simulator; added flakeguard and made test deterministic.
- Final CI run: all checks passed (unit, integration, e2e-canary on staging).

Manual testing and incident rehearsal: 
- Ran staged canary (10% of traffic) for 24 hours against staging cluster while generating tenant-localized bursts. Observed: ADMO applied priority trims to identified low-cost cohorts, preserved latency for VIP tenants, and avoided circuit flips during 3 simulated overloads. KV-preserve drains completed in >95% of evict-invocations vs 70% baseline.

Rollout and rollback plan: 
- Enable behind feature flag: admode.enabled=false by default.
- Rollout path: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 3 days with automated metric checks: regional-p95, canary-error-rate, kv-drain-success-rate.
- Automatic pause: if canary error-rate increases > 0.5% absolute or kv-drain-success-rate drops below 85%, the rollout pauses and a rollback job runs to disable ADMO.

Release notes (for changelog):
- "Add experimental Adaptive Degraded Mode Operator for SLO-aware admission control and a Priority Triage Probe to classify burst traffic. Improves regional stability during tenant-localized spikes; opt-in behind a feature flag. Includes observability and rollout recipes."

Follow-ups (not included in this PR):
- Policy DSL for ADMO rules (ENG-4502).
- SDK hooks so customers can surface priority tags to downstream telemetry.

Merge details:
- Merge method: squash and merge.
- Commit message condensed to: "admission: adaptive degraded-mode operator + priority triage probe; telemetry sanitizer; ops rollout"

Contact / On-call:
- Primary owner: Maya Patel (runtime team).
- Slack channel: #runtime-admode.

Notes for on-call: when investigating ADMO-induced soft-deny events, start with the admode-overview dashboard and confirm quorum-health. If quorum-health is stale, the system will revert to static shedder; escalate to runtime if reversion does not happen within 20s.

End of PR description.
commit_message: admission: adaptive degraded-mode operator + priority triage probe; telemetry sanitizer; ops rollout
